results.content: A Pennsylvania man who fatally shot eight others, including seven family members, before killing himself had exercised strict control over his relatives, including their finances and interactions with others, police said Thursday. results.content: The Federal Reserve’s latest Survey of Consumer Finances revealed a striking split: Median net worth rose roughly 38% for households headed by someone 75 or older between 2022 and 2025, while falling 23% for those headed by someone under 35. Americans 55 and over now hold roughly $140 trillion, about three-quarters of the nation’s net worth, *Fortune* reported this month, citing a Bank of America Institute analysis of the Fed data. results.content: Consumer sentiment inched down this month, eroded by worries that persistent inflation will further weaken buying power, the University of Michigan said Friday in a survey report. [...] Household perceptions of the conditions for purchasing durable goods slumped 18% because of concerns about rising interest rates and declining affordability, Joanne Hsu, the university’s surveys of consumers director, said in a statement. With less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 mid-term elections, a decline in sentiment among independent voters exceeded an increase in the outlook among Republicans and Democrats.
results.title: Consumer sentiment dips on worries about affordability: UMichigan survey

results.content: The September reading of the University of Michigan’s monthly Index of Consumer Sentiment marked only the fourth time in the survey's history, dating back to 1952, that the index dropped below 50, with the other three occasions coming between April and June of this year.
